summary: Keep private .local state usable without letting it become a dependency of shared project behavior.

prerequisites: Identify the repository root, applicable instructions, and the requested operation involving .local.
outcomes: Resolve the private boundary even when .local does not exist yet.
Choose private, shared, promotion, or outside-repository handling for each operation.
Prevent private files and workarounds from entering tracked configuration, tooling, packages, or product behavior.

scenarios.title: Create private state for the first time
scenarios.prompt: Use the protect-local-boundary skill before creating a new .local workspace in this Git repository.
scenarios.outcome: The absent directory is treated as private, locally excluded before creation, and kept independent from tracked project configuration.

scenarios.title: Promote one input without watcher leakage
scenarios.prompt: Use the protect-local-boundary skill to turn one approved file from .local into a project asset while a repository-wide development watcher is active.
scenarios.outcome: Only the approved item becomes a self-contained project asset, while temporary work stays outside the repository and shared tooling remains independent from .local.
